case_title: Manoj and Anr. v. State of Karnataka
accused_victim_relationship: Prior enmity/dispute: the victim suspected an illicit intimacy between one accused and his wife, had forbidden that accused from visiting, and threatened to kill him
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 r/w s.34; IPC s.506 r/w s.34 (charged); IPC s.325 (substituted for appellant No.2)
evidence_type: Eyewitness (PWs 8, 16, 18); medical (post-mortem); forensic (FSL report on blood on sword and stone); recovery/seizure (site plan and seizures by police)
aggravating_circumstances: Use of a sword; gruesome assault; multiple injuries including a fatal neck injury
mitigating_circumstances: For appellant No.2: his role was limited to throwing a stone; no evidence of intent to kill or pre-concert; no motive attributed to him; long period in jail
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302 r/w s.34 IPC: life imprisonment and fine of Rs.10,000 each; convicted under s.506 r/w s.34 IPC: one year simple imprisonment and fine of Rs.2,000 each
high_court_outcome: Conviction and sentence under s.302 r/w s.34 affirmed; conviction and sentence under s.506 r/w s.34 set aside
offence_finally_established: Murder (IPC s.302) for appellant No.1 (Manoj); grievous hurt (IPC s.325) for appellant No.2
neutral_facts: The prosecution case is that the victim disliked a man visiting his house and suspected him of having an illicit relationship with the victim's wife. The victim had forbidden the man from coming to the house and threatened to kill him if he returned. About two days before the incident the man came again and the victim repeated the threat. On the day of the incident, around noon, the victim was sitting in front of a roadside eatery near a bus stand. Two witnesses had just finished taking tea there and saw a verbal altercation between the victim and two accused, one of whom was the man's father. During the altercation, one accused threw a stone which struck the victim on the head. The victim fell, and the other accused struck him several times with a sword, injuring his neck, head and face. People nearby ran away. Witnesses said the attackers fled believing the victim dead. Witnesses tried to help the victim, who was bleeding heavily, and took him to a police station and then toward a hospital, where he died en route. Police witnesses prepared a site plan and seized items from the spot, including the sword and the stone. The post-mortem found several ante-mortem external injuries, including a frontal bone fracture, a crush injury to the cheek, and a neck wound with a vertebral fracture. The doctor opined the injuries were sufficient to cause death in the ordinary course. The doctor stated that the crush injury could be caused by the stone and the other injuries by the sword. A forensic report found human blood on the blade of the sword and on the stone.
physical_harm: Death of the victim. Ante-mortem injuries: cut wound over right eye with frontal bone fracture; crush injury to left cheek; cut wound at left angle of mouth; wrist wound; neck wound with C2 vertebra fracture
number_of_offences: 2 charged (IPC s.302 r/w s.34; IPC s.506 r/w s.34); 1 finally upheld (s.302 for appellant No.1), with s.325 substituted for appellant No.2
premeditation_planning: Not found; the court noted no evidence of pre-concert between the two accused to kill the victim
motive: Accepted: the victim's suspicion of an illicit intimacy between one accused and his wife. No motive attributed to the other accused, as the prosecution did not allege one against him.
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness testimony of PWs 8, 18 and 16 on the sequence of events; testimony on prior threats and suspected illicit intimacy; post-mortem evidence; FSL report showing blood on sword and stone; site plan and seizure evidence of police witnesses
witness_credibility: PWs 8, 18 and 16 found reliable and consistent; their testimony survived lengthy cross-examination. PWs 4, 5, 7, 17 and 19 turned hostile and gave no support to the prosecution.
post_offence_conduct: Fled the scene after the assault, believing the victim dead (as stated in PW-18's testimony; not separately found by the court)
custody_duration: Appellant No.2: nearly 3½ years in jail at the time of the judgment. Appellant No.1: not stated.
trial_duration: offence: 30 August 2006; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 15 November 2011; Supreme Court: 5 July 2013
legal_representation: Appellants: H. Chandra Sekhar. State/Respondent: C.B. Gururaj and V.N. Raghupathy.
investigation_status: Case registered; charge-sheet filed; trial completed with 22 prosecution witnesses examined
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under ss.302 and 506 r/w s.34 IPC. High Court: s.302/34 conviction affirmed; s.506/34 set aside. Supreme Court: appeal of appellant No.1 dismissed; appellant No.2's conviction altered to s.325 IPC.
prosecution_argument: Not stated (the judgment records no separate prosecution submissions in the Supreme Court)
defence_argument: Appellant No.2's role was restricted to throwing a stone; nothing showed that the stone was intended to kill or that the assault continued after it; no pre-concert to kill
legal_principle_applied: Murder under s.302 (including via s.34) requires intention to cause death or a shared intention to do so; absent such evidence, liability is limited to the accused's own role, here grievous hurt under s.325. Eyewitness and medical evidence assessed for reliability.
sentencing_rationale: For appellant No.2: the sentence of nearly 3½ years already undergone was held sufficient given his limited role and conviction altered to s.325 IPC
judicial_mitigating_factors: For appellant No.2: the stone may have triggered the incident but there was no intent to kill; he was involved in an initial altercation; time already served
judicial_aggravating_factors: For appellant No.1: use of a sword to inflict fatal injuries in a gruesome assault
other_sentence_order: Appellant No.2 to be released from custody unless required in another case; fine imposed on appellant No.2 remains unaltered
